name: wadefagen/datasets
what_it_holds: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) open datasets as committed CSVs: uiuc-gpa-dataset.csv (course GPA distributions by Year/Term back to Fall 2016), uiuc-tre-dataset.csv (teacher ratings), uiuc-geneds-dataset.csv, uiuc-students-by-state.csv (student counts broken out by home US state), uiuc-course-catalog.csv, and illini-football-scores.csv. All keyed by Year/Term (Spring/Summer/Fall/Winter) with a combined YearTerm field.
why_useful: students-by-state plus the by-term enrollment counts give a real, single-campus panel of term-level student population and home-state mix that could be used as a toy proxy for term-start/term-end travel volume and out-of-state (i.e., travel-generating) student share; useful mainly as a methods template for building a similar panel across more campuses, not itself a multi-university dataset.

name: edgartools
what_it_holds: Python client (MIT, 2711 stars, active, updated 2026-09-14) that reads and structures the full SEC EDGAR archive back to 1994: 10-K/10-Q financial statements, XBRL-standardized concepts for cross-company comparison, 8-K events, 13F institutional holdings, Form 3/4/5 insider transactions, DEF 14A proxies, fund N-CSR/N-PORT reports. Not a static dataset -- a one-command pull tool for point-in-time filing data (filing timestamps are inherent to EDGAR, so this can build vintage-correct financial statement panels for ABNB/BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT and institutional-ownership history) without XBRL frames plumbing.
why_useful: General-purpose, no-cost way to pull point-in-time XBRL facts for NCLH/CCL/RCL — including custom tags cruise lines use for 'Advance ticket sales' / deferred revenue — quarter by quarter, which is exactly the book-ahead analogue metric gap #18 wants. Also usable for point-in-time company_filings_estimates work generally (gap #4).
time_coverage: as far back as each company's EDGAR XBRL history goes (typically 2009+)
themes: Cruise line data: NCLH / Carnival / Royal Caribbean advance ticket sales, capacity, occupancy, cruise schedules and port calls
SEC EDGAR tooling: full-text search, 8-K/10-Q parsers, XBRL frames, financial statement datasets, edgar-crawler; peer print scrapers (BKNG EXPE MAR HLT)
13F holdings parsers and institutional-ownership history, short-interest datasets, insider-transaction parsers (Form 4), ETF holdings trackers
Event-study and factor packages; earnings-surprise datasets; post-earnings-drift replication; Ken French factor loaders
wildcard: a sell-side analyst covering online travel who assembles con
why_all: General-purpose, no-cost way to pull point-in-time XBRL facts for NCLH/CCL/RCL — including custom tags cruise lines use for 'Advance ticket sales' / deferred revenue — quarter by quarter, which is exactly the book-ahead analogue metric gap #18 wants. Also usable for point-in-time company_filings_estimates work generally (gap #4).

Could point-in-time-pull BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT (and ABNB) XBRL financials and 8-K exhibits quarter by quarter for the peer-print comparison the team already tracks (gap 15: SEC EDGAR XBRL tooling); also usable to backfill ABNB's own XBRL history with clean field names instead of hand-parsing filings.

One-command point-in-time pull of ABNB/BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT XBRL financials and 8-K exhibits (KPI tables) straight from EDGAR, and could backfill the guidance ledger / peer-8-K-KPI table with an exact filing-date timestamp for gap 4 (point-in-time consensus/financials) and gap 15 (XBRL tooling).

General-purpose, well-maintained method to pull ABNB's own 13F institutional-ownership history (concentration/turnover of holders) and any Form 4 insider transactions for ABNB officers/directors -- directly addresses gap #15 (company-structure signals: 13F parsers, concentration history, SEC EDGAR tooling).

Could mechanize pulling ABNB's (and peers' BKNG/EXPE/MAR/HLT) historical 8-K earnings-release dates and XBRL figures point-in-time, and cross-check against the existing guidance ledger/press-quote consensus register -- addresses gap #15 (SEC EDGAR full-text/XBRL tooling).

Directly serves gap #15 (13F holdings, EDGAR XBRL tooling) and the point-in-time consensus/financials need in #4 -- gives an easy, well-maintained way to pull vintage-correct peer financials and 13F ownership snapshots at each historical filing date rather than pull-date-anchored Bloomberg exports.

name: BNPL_Merchant_Dataset
what_it_holds: Research pipeline scraping the official BNPL provider merchant directories (Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay, Zip, Sezzle) for merchant name/category/provider/URL, matched via SEC ticker files + SEC CompanyFacts API to public parent companies, building a quarterly firm-panel 2015-2026. Current checkpoint: 8,470 unique merchants, 144 public-company merchant rows / 127 unique parents, 4,675 firm-fiscal-quarter SEC records (93.6% revenue coverage), adoption-date verification via Internet Archive CDX (no fabricated dates, unresolved dates left UNKNOWN).
why_useful: Directly on-theme: a maintained, methodologically careful cross-reference of which public companies (and whether Airbnb-adjacent travel merchants) accept which BNPL provider, plus the SEC-filing financial panel around adoption timing - this is the closest thing found to 'is Airbnb/travel-lodging a BNPL merchant and when did BNPL options appear' with a reusable, non-fabricated methodology. Also a template for checking Airbnb's own presence in Affirm/Klarna merchant directories.
geography: US (SEC-filer universe), BNPL provider directories are broader
time_coverage: merchant directories current; SEC financial panel 2015-2026
themes: Consumer credit and BNPL: Klarna/Affirm public stats, Fed G.19, credit card delinquency, CFPB complaints dataset (Airbnb refund complaints), BBB complaint scrapers
why_all: Directly on-theme: a maintained, methodologically careful cross-reference of which public companies (and whether Airbnb-adjacent travel merchants) accept which BNPL provider, plus the SEC-filing financial panel around adoption timing - this is the closest thing found to 'is Airbnb/travel-lodging a BNPL merchant and when did BNPL options appear' with a reusable, non-fabricated methodology. name: MAEC dataset
what_it_holds: Multimodal Aligned Earnings Conference call corpus, S&P 1500 companies, described as 6x larger than prior academic sets. In-repo: transcripts + low-level audio (CSV) features, 147.7MB, organized YearMonthDay_CompanyCode/text.txt+features.csv. High-level MFCC features (59GB, .npy) hosted on Google Drive. Includes forced-alignment Python code (Python 3.5, pydub/aeneas/ffmpeg). CIKM 2020 paper; CC-BY-SA-4.0 license; 107 stars, 25 forks, 17 commits.
why_useful: Largest open academic multimodal earnings-call corpus (S&P 1500) with a permissive share-alike license; usable both as a peer-tone benchmark and as a worked example of a text+audio alignment pipeline that could, in principle, be pointed at ABNB's own call audio/transcripts.
size_hint: 147.7MB in-repo text+CSV features; 59GB audio features via Google Drive
last_activity: 17 commits, exact date not surfaced; 107 stars
themes: Earnings-call transcript datasets and NLP tooling (ECT datasets, Motley Fool scrapers, Seeking Alpha parsers), management-tone corpora
why_all: Largest open academic multimodal earnings-call corpus (S&P 1500) with a permissive share-alike license; usable both as a peer-tone benchmark and as a worked example of a text+audio alignment pipeline that could, in principle, be pointed at ABNB's own call audio/transcripts.
